title: Observability ops scenario matrix and panel slimming notes
content:
Context and objective:
This is a working note for a compact, incident-driven observability surface. Goal: map common operational scenarios to a minimal set of metrics + trace anchors + dashboard panels, then propose a practical panel-slimming strategy to reduce noise and query cost while keeping effective signal for fast triage.

Why this doc (short):
- Observability dashboards have grown organically; query cost and operator cognitive load are rising.
- We need an ops-centric matrix (scenario -> signals -> single-panel equivalents) so oncall can find the right evidence quickly.
- Also propose concrete panel culling heuristics and short PromQL/SQL snippets for key signals.

High-level scenario matrix (compact):
- Scenario: Burst latency for hosted API (sudden p99 spike)
  - Primary metrics: request-rate (r/s), token-p99-latency-ms, model-queue-depth, kv_cache_hit_ratio_windowed (60s)
  - Tracing anchors: request.session_id, model.variant, route.policy, kvcache.lookup (hit/miss)
  - Short dashboard panel: single timeseries, stacked heatmap of request-rate vs p99 latency with an overlay for kv cache hit ratio
  - Quick hypothesis checklist: capacity saturation vs cache coldness vs slow model kernel

- Scenario: Increased error-rate (5xx) confined to a subset of tenants
  - Primary metrics: error-rate-per-tenant (% over 5m), backend-5xx-count, model-fallback-rate, tenant-cpu-usage
  - Tracing anchors: tenant.id, request.route_id, fallback.reason, backend.instance_id
  - Panel: grouped bar showing top 10 tenants by error-rate + a breadcrumbs trace sampler linked to top offenders

- Scenario: Quality regression (CTR/downstream metric drop after rollout)
  - Primary metrics: eval-prompt-set-failure-rate, rerank-hits-per-1000, top-level-application-telemetry (ingestion of eval samples)
  - Tracing anchors: model.commit_hash, rollout.flag, prompt.eval_id
  - Panel: small table showing before/after eval-metrics (baseline vs current) + trace sample links for failing prompts

- Scenario: KV cache degenerating (cold/cascading misses)
  - Primary metrics: kv_cache_hit_ratio_windowed (1m, 5m), prefix-warmth-score (see def), token-amortized-cost, cache-eviction-rate
  - Tracing anchors: session.kv_prefix, kvcache.version, model.context_length
  - Panel: dual-axis timeseries (hit ratio + eviction rate) with histogram of prefix length distribution

Metric definitions (proposal, names should be stable):
- request.rate.rps: rate(requests_total[1m]) per route/model (float string)
- token.p99.latency.ms: 99th percentile token-latency (end-to-end generation) aggregated by model & route (ms)
- kv_cache_hit_ratio_windowed: (kvcache_hits[60s] / (kvcache_hits[60s] + kvcache_misses[60s])) * 100 — windowed to capture transient churn
- prefix-warmth-score: weighted fraction of requests that find prefix length >= X (X = 64 tokens by default) in the cache in the last 5m (0-1)
- routing.fallback.rate: count(fallbacks) / count(requests) over 5m (useful for capacity/fallback health)
- model.variant.latency.delta: token.p95.latency(model_variant) - token.p95.latency(baseline_variant)

Tracing anchor recommendations (span tags / attributes to prioritize):
- request.session_id (guid) — required on all entry spans
- request.route_id (string) — high-cardinality but essential for tenant separation
- model.variant and model.commit_hash — for rollout correlation
- kvcache.hit boolean and kvcache.lookup_time_ms — trace-level detail to explain latency spikes
- fallback.reason (enum) — must be short values (capacity, incompatible, error)

Sampling strategy (pragmatic):
- Always-sample traces for full requests when p95/p99 latency crosses threshold OR when fallback.reason != null.
- Target baseline sampling 0.5% of normal traffic per-model, with spike-bucket booster (sample 10% of requests for 30m after an alert incident).
- Privacy: redact PII fields at ingest (client-provided text) and keep only structured prompt hashes / eval ids.

Panel slimming heuristics (practical steps):
1) Panel heat ranking: compute (query-cost * top-10-view-count) and rank panels; consider culling bottom 30% by impact score.
2) Replace dense multi-queries with small derived metrics (pre-aggregations) for common triage flows (e.g., kv_cache_hit_ratio_windowed).
3) Promote single-source-of-truth time-series per scenario (one primary panel) and hide others in a collapsed "investigate" section.
4) Move heavyweight tables / histograms to "on-demand" widgets (link out to a short-run notebook or ad-hoc query) instead of default dashboard.
5) Ownership tags: add panel metadata tag owner:team/person and a "cost-est" label (low/med/high). Panels without owners for > 90 days are candidates for removal.

Suggested alert thresholds (starting points, tune per-model):
- token.p99.latency.ms per-route > baseline * 2 for 5m -> P1
- routing.fallback.rate > 5% for 10m -> P2 (investigate capacity/policy mismatch)
- kv_cache_hit_ratio_windowed < 60% for 10m -> P2 (cache warmup or eviction issue)
- request-rate drop > 30% across region for 5m with no infra events -> P1 (ingestion outage)

PromQL / SQL snippets (quick starters):
- kv cache hit ratio (PromQL style):
  sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total[1m])) by (model) / (sum(rate(kvcache_hits_total[1m]) + rate(kvcache_misses_total[1m])) by (model))

- p99 token latency (PromQL suggestion):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))

- top tenants by 5xx (SQL-like):
  SELECT tenant_id, count(*) as errors_5xx FROM requests WHERE status >= 500 AND timestamp > now() - interval '5 minutes' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY errors_5xx DESC LIMIT 10;

Operational runbook snippets (mini):
- If p99 latency spikes: check model queue depth -> check kvcache hit ratio -> check recent deploys/rollouts -> sample traces for slow spans (kvcache.lookup_time_ms vs model.kernel_execute_ms).
- If localized tenant 5xx: route requests to fallback pool (if configured) -> capture traces for a sample of failing requests -> escalate to platform infra if instance OOM or similar.

Open questions / follow-ups (TODOs):
- Finalize prefix-warmth-score bucket boundaries and name.
- Add a lightweight panel cost sampler in dashboards to surface query cost per widget (prototype needed).
- Decide retention tiers for trace attributes (full trace vs index-only) across Dedicated vs Hosted customers.
- Add an "investigation-mode" dashboard template with collapsed panels and quick query links for oncall.

References and quick links:
- confluence:OBS-MATRIX-128 (design notes)
- jira:OBS-4123 (panel-cost instrumentation ticket)
- github:repo/observability/dashboards#45 (prototype slim-dashboard change)

Notes to self:
- Keep examples small and copyable.
- Try to land prefix-warmth metric as a derived metric in ingestion pipeline (cheap to compute).

-- Aisha
